questions.q: What is Northbridge Retail's checkout service built with, and why does its load differ from product-catalog's?
options: Node.js and Express; its load is steady because product browsing never spikes
Python and FastAPI; its load is spiky because of flash sales driving order submission
Go and gRPC; its load is steady because it only runs nightly batch jobs
Java and Spring; its load is spiky because of scheduled Postgres backups
questions.explain: Checkout is a Python 3.12 + FastAPI service. Because flash sales drive bursts of order submissions, its traffic is much higher and spikier than product-catalog's steady read traffic.

questions.q: Which external dependencies does the checkout service call when processing an order?
options: Only the Postgres database
PaymentPro for payment and an existing legacy inventory service to check stock
A second copy of product-catalog running in the same namespace
Azure Key Vault directly for every request
questions.explain: Checkout calls out to PaymentPro (OAuth2 client-credentials) for payment and to an already-running legacy inventory service to confirm stock, then hands the order to a shipping carrier via webhook.

questions.q: In the end-to-end architecture, what happens immediately after a PR is squash-merged to main?
options: Nothing — a human must manually trigger the dev deploy
The change auto-deploys straight to production
An image is built and pushed to the shared registry, then automatically deployed to the northbridge-dev namespace
The change is automatically promoted to staging without a tag
questions.explain: Merging to main triggers CI to push an image (tagged with the git SHA) to the shared ACR and then helm upgrade --install into the northbridge-dev namespace — automatically, with no tag or approval required.

questions.q: What triggers promotion to the staging namespace, and what gates promotion from staging to production?
options: A tag push triggers staging; prod requires a manual approval gate (GitHub Environments, 1 required reviewer)
Staging and prod are both fully automatic with no gates
A merge to main triggers staging; a tag push triggers prod with no approval needed
Both staging and prod require a manual approval gate
questions.explain: A maintainer cutting a semver tag (e.g. v1.4.0) auto-deploys to staging. Moving from staging to prod requires a manual approval gate enforced via a GitHub Environments protection rule with one required reviewer.

questions.q: How are monitoring and security positioned relative to the four capstone phases?
options: They are the subject of Phase 1 only, before any infrastructure exists
They are skipped entirely in this capstone to keep scope manageable
They are layered across every environment and pipeline stage, not a separate add-on phase at the end
They only apply to the production namespace, not dev or staging
questions.explain: Prometheus/Grafana/Alertmanager monitor all three namespaces, and Trivy, gitleaks, Checkov, Key Vault, and GitHub OIDC protect every stage of the pipeline — they run underneath the whole system, not as a final bolt-on.
